name: room
text: Room opened — goal: improve: Self-improvement: review prompts/engines/routing/own-code; auto-apply safe changes; pitch

name: Sprocket
text: Run PR-Agent in shadow mode on the newest merged PR first. It’s the fastest way to validate its feedback loop against real-world merges without risking open PRs. The trade-off is delayed feedback on open PRs, but merged PRs are safer to test against since they’re already approved.

name: Gauge
text: Shadow mode on merged PRs only catches errors *after* they’re already in product—it’s a post-mortem, not prevention. A better test is running PR-Agent in shadow mode on *open* PRs first; that catches issues before they ship, not after. Settle it by comparing error rates in production vs. open PRs after a week of each approach.

name: Overhaul
text: Run PR-Agent in shadow mode on the newest *open* PR first, then expand to merged PRs—this catches issues before they ship, cutting post-mortem fixes. Start with one PR to validate the feedback loop before scaling, reducing wasted effort on misconfigured rules.

name: Sprocket
text: Run PR-Agent in shadow mode on the newest open PR first. This catches routing flaws and review gaps before they ship, cutting post-mortem fixes. The trade-off is accepting zero risk to the open PR while we validate the feedback loop. Once it proves reliable on one PR, we scale to merged PRs for broader coverage. This balances prevention with safety.
